tasks.short: Review and draft material risk disclosures for offer documents.

steps.what: Gather offer terms, financial figures and current exposure records.
Retrieve approved clauses, previous disclosures and disclosure requirements.
Determine which risks are material and how the offer changes exposure.
Draft risk disclosures using the assessment, evidence and approved wording.

loop.input: Material risk assessment, offer evidence pack and versioned disclosure reference pack.
loop.output: Draft risk disclosure with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check figures and clause versions deterministically; the risk specialist checks meaning, omissions and source support.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per section; unsupported claims become questions for manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but offer-specific risks require supported prose across several documents.

steps.what: Review completeness, legal wording and factual support; approve the disclosure.
Send the approved disclosure and its version reference to the offer document owner.

tasks.design: An integration assembles versioned evidence from the {ERP} and {DOCS}, while configured retrieval selects approved reference material. A bounded drafting loop produces source-linked sections in {DOCS} after the specialist determines material risks; {WORKFLOW} records legal approval and sends the approved version through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Offer-specific wording and materiality resist fixed templates. Evidence, clause versions and approvals often sit in separate files.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding reduces the effort of building evidence assembly and validation. Bounded drafting can use approved wording and explicit source references.
tasks.still_hard: Materiality, misleading omissions and legal interpretation remain expensive to assess. Confidential information needs controlled access under GDPR; EU AI Act obligations depend on the use.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a material risk that standard clauses obscure, and explaining its significance without misleading the reader.
tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time collecting evidence and assembling prose, and more time testing material risks before offer terms settle. They gain an earlier advisory role; disclosure approval remains with legal counsel.

reach.task: Map disclosure requirements to supporting evidence.
reach.learn: Learn requirement applicability, evidence sufficiency and document retention.

reach.task: Assess how proposed offer terms change financial exposure.
reach.learn: Learn funding structure, financial commitments and management risk appetite.

evidence.claim: Document assembly, version checks and approval routing can use deterministic technology.
Moody's Credit Memo drafts credit memos from financial spreads, deal documents and templates; this supports an adjacent drafting pattern.
A published spreadsheet-agent benchmark found incorrect cash-waterfall results, supporting independent numerical checks.

assumptions: This task applies to a mid-size issuer or financial business producing offer documents.
Reference clauses and disclosure requirements can be versioned in the {DOCS}.
The offer document owner handles external publication after this task.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
The access range includes consultation where national rules apply; formal consent processes may take longer.
unknowns: Offer types, jurisdictions and applicable disclosure requirements.
Who holds final disclosure approval authority.
Availability of approved clauses and reliable exposure records.
Permitted model hosting, retention and access arrangements.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for this change.
research_questions: Which disclosure sections can use fixed clauses without losing offer-specific meaning?
How often does a source-linked draft omit a material risk?
Which factual checks can block an unsupported draft before legal review?
new_work: Review generated wording and resolve unsupported statements.
Maintain clause versions, requirement mappings and source access.
Handle missing evidence and changed offer terms.
Sample approved disclosures for omissions and traceability failures.

tasks.short: Measure market exposure for traded instruments and report breaches, changes and recommended responses.

steps.what: Retrieve traded positions and transaction changes from the treasury system.
Retrieve prices, rates and instrument reference data from the market data service.
Match instruments, reconcile positions and flag missing or stale market data.
Calculate exposure and sensitivity measures in the treasury risk system.
Assess material changes and agree escalation priorities with the treasury manager.
Compile risk figures, charts and agreed commentary into the reporting pack.
Distribute the report and notify internal owners of approved escalations.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile position and market data from the {OTHER}, with unresolved inputs quarantined. Configured calculations in the {OTHER} feed a {BI} dashboard and deterministic report generator in {DOCS}; {WORKFLOW} routes material escalations for approval and sends notifications through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instrument identifiers, valuation timestamps and data licences complicate integration. Spreadsheet reconciliation and reporting bridge gaps between existing systems.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding reduces the cost of adapters, reconciliation rules and report templates. Existing risk calculations can be scheduled without a model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Illiquid prices, complex instruments and methodology validation remain difficult. Data licensing and reliable timestamps can dominate costs.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when reported exposure understates liquidity risk, correlation changes or a misleading market price.
tasks.altitude: The specialist shifts from assembling reporting packs to investigating exceptions and testing stress assumptions. They can prioritise investigations within agreed thresholds; trading and limit changes retain existing approval rights.

reach.task: Assess liquidity and hedging responses to market exposure.
reach.learn: Learn funding constraints, hedge execution costs and liquidity buffers.

reach.task: Maintain reconciled exposure datasets and risk dashboards.
reach.learn: Learn data lineage, valuation timestamps and instrument identifier mapping.

evidence.claim: Position reconciliation, exposure arithmetic, limit checks and structured reporting can use deterministic technology.
Existing treasury risk software commonly supports scheduled metrics; availability must be confirmed locally.
Baker Tilly Netherlands reported faster statement tie-outs using DataSnipper; this is adjacent audit evidence, not a market-risk savings estimate.
A published spreadsheet-agent benchmark found numerical errors, supporting deterministic calculations and independent reconciliation.

assumptions: The company has a traded portfolio or treasury exposures requiring regular monitoring.
The {OTHER} covers treasury risk systems and licensed market data services.
The treasury risk system already implements the approved exposure measures.
Unresolved data exceptions block affected calculations; reports label incomplete coverage.
Estimates cover one portfolio and existing measures, not a new risk methodology or market data licence.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability are assessed for the actual use; this design contains no model loop.
The access range includes consultation where national rules apply; formal consent processes may take longer.
unknowns: Portfolio size, instrument complexity and reporting frequency.
Available interfaces, scheduling features and market data usage rights.
Approved risk measures, thresholds and escalation authority.
Current reconciliation failures and manual override practices.
Whether personal data or employee monitoring enters the workflow.
Whether national rules require employee consultation.
research_questions: Which existing calculations and reports can be scheduled through configuration?
What timestamp and identifier rules prevent false exposure changes?
Which instruments require manual valuation or additional stress analysis?
new_work: Resolve unmatched instruments, stale prices and reconciliation failures.
Maintain adapters, mappings, thresholds and report templates.
Validate calculation changes against approved reference results.
Investigate material breaches and record escalation decisions.
Monitor failed runs, coverage gaps and data licence changes.

role.altitude: The week shifts toward materiality assessment, exposure investigation and earlier advice on offer terms. The specialist gains scope to prioritise analysis and propose responses; legal approval, trading authority and risk-limit approval remain with their designated owners.
reach: Compliance Officers: connect disclosure obligations to evidence.
Treasurers and Controllers: connect exposure changes to liquidity and hedging choices.
Business Intelligence Analysts: connect risk reporting to governed data and lineage.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a pre-offer disclosure gap assessment and daily liquidity-adjusted exposure escalation using shared, traceable evidence.
